caption:
When your child falls, the first thing out of our mouths is usually "Are you okay?!" But little ones look at our faces to decide how scary something was. A panicked question teaches them to read YOUR fear before they check their own body.

Instead, pause, stay calm and observe. Try saying:

🙏 "Whoa, that was a big fall! You landed on your hands."

🙏 "I saw that. Do you need a hug, or are you ready to keep going?"

🙏 "That surprised you! Take a breath. What does your body need?"

Here's why this matters more than you think:

✅ They learn to check their own body instead of copying your panic
✅ They learn to name what they feel: scared, surprised, sore
✅ They get the choice to be comforted or to get back up
✅ You become a calm guide, not a worried rescuer
✅ They learn early that God holds them, even when they fall

"Though he fall, he shall not be cast headlong, for the LORD upholds his hand." Psalm 37:24

We all fall. Jesus came for people who fall, and He's the One who lifts us back up.

The goal isn't a child who never falls.
It's a child who knows how to get back up. 💪
